title: 2023 capital budget direction to staff
subtitle: Interim tax levy by-law, a January 27 joint education session at RIM Park, and a councillor's conflict disclosure.
overview: Council held a short special meeting to set direction on the 2023 capital budget. It asked staff to return with more information on several items raised at the earlier Special Finance and Corporate Services Committee meeting {{vote:m1}}. These include borrowing from reserves instead of issuing debt, the effect of cutting urban forestry funding, more money for two neighbourhood grant programs, and moving cycling money to trail paving.

No budget amounts were approved at this meeting. The direction only asks for reports, so the final spending choices will come later. One councillor declared a pecuniary interest in two engineering reconstruction projects (Mill Street and Connaught Street) and did not take part in any discussion or vote on them.

Council also authorized a closed session on Friday, January 27 at RIM Park, held with the Region of Waterloo and other local municipalities, to receive education and training {{vote:m2}}. Council gave three readings to a by-law setting the 2023 interim tax levy and to the by-law confirming the day's proceedings {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.detail: Staff are to provide more information on borrowing internally from reserves rather than issuing debt, including the existing Capital Funding & Debt policy.
Staff are to report on the impact of reducing the Urban Forestry budget by $100,000 a year, $1M in total.

decisions.item: RISE and Love My Hood grants
decisions.detail: Staff are to report on increasing funding to the RISE and Love My Hood grants and how the increase would be funded.
Staff are to report on moving $300,000 a year from cycling infrastructure to paving trails.

decisions.item: Grand River Park and park garbage
decisions.detail: Staff are to report on resources and costs to develop Grand River Park and on enhanced garbage collection options in parks and trails.
Staff are to report on the Council Home Technology budget and whether it remains adequate for the term of Council.

debate: The meeting had little debate. The capital budget direction was moved, seconded and carried after the chair asked for discussion and none was recorded in the transcript.
A councillor disclosed a pecuniary interest in two engineering projects, saying family members own property nearby. The councillor noted this should have been raised at the committee stage.

The chair said the disclosure was still required even though council was not endorsing projects at this meeting. The chair asked for the paperwork to be filed and said it would be needed again on budget day.
